metadata.title: Guide to Analyzing and Reporting Tribes in Pol.is Conversations
metadata.purpose: Generate consistent, evidence-based reports comparing tribes and describing the key differences between them

criticalInstructions.instruction: Generate a JSON response that conforms to the provided schema. DO NOT INCLUDE ANY OTHER TEXT.
DO NOT return ```json at the beginning of the response. This is not markdown. Do not end the response with ```, your response MUST begin with { and end with }

CRITICAL DATA VERIFICATION: Before writing ANY claim about how a tribe voted on a statement, you MUST check the actual vote data. - Use the per-group vote attributes (group-0 agrees, group-1 agrees, etc.) to determine each tribe's actual position - NEVER claim a tribe disagreed with a statement if the data shows they agreed - NEVER claim a statement divided tribes if all tribes show similar voting patterns - Your narrative must be fully grounded in the actual numbers

term.name: group_differences
term.description: Notable difference in views between tribes, especially comments where tribes disagreed significantly

term.name: extreme_differences
term.description: Very large difference in views between tribes (typically where one tribe strongly agrees and another strongly disagrees)

criticalInstructions.instruction: Focus on the full set of tribes, not just pairs of tribes. Describe the constellation of views across all tribes.
Use specific statements to illustrate tribe positions, but do so in service of showing broader patterns rather than isolated points.
Avoid generic descriptions. Instead, characterize each tribe by their distinctive positions and apparent priorities or values.

paragraph.format:
Analysis of voting patterns revealed [number_of_groups] distinct tribes with different perspectives on key issues. These tribes were primarily defined by their positions on [key_division_theme], particularly regarding [specific_aspect]. [Additional_high_level_context].
The most significant divisions between tribes emerged around [major_division_topic], with [description_of_key_disagreement]. This reflected deeper differences in [values/priorities/concerns], especially in discussions of [related_subtopic]. [Additional_insight_if_relevant].
[If extreme polarization exists] Particularly stark contrasts appeared in positions on [polarizing_topic], where Tribes [X] and [Y] took [diametrically_opposed_positions] on [specific_statements]. This division highlighted fundamental differences in [underlying_values_or_frameworks].

paragraphInstructions.instruction: Provide a comprehensive overview that: - Introduces all identified tribes - Highlights major lines of division - Connects specific differences to broader themes - Avoids overemphasizing any single statement or division - Provides multiple specific examples with appropriate citations

criticalInstructions.instruction: For each key division, explain both WHAT tribes disagree about AND WHY they likely disagree (different values, priorities, assumptions, etc.). Avoid simplistic explanations.
Draw connections between different points of disagreement to reveal patterns in tribe thinking, not just isolated differences.
Be precise in characterizing each tribe's position. Avoid reducing complex stances to simple agree/disagree dichotomies when more nuanced patterns exist.

paragraph.format:
Tribe [A], comprising approximately [percentage_estimate]% of participants, demonstrated strong [agreement/disagreement] with statements addressing [topic_X]. Their voting pattern revealed consistent emphasis on [value_or_priority], particularly regarding [specific_aspect]. This was most evident in their [strong/moderate] [agreement/disagreement] with statements about [specific_subtopic].
In contrast, Tribe [B] prioritized [different_value_or_priority], consistently supporting positions that [description_of_position]. This tribe's perspective was characterized by [distinctive_feature_of_voting_pattern], especially on statements related to [topic_Y]. Their approach to [shared_topic] differed fundamentally from Tribe [A] in terms of [specific_dimension_of_difference].
Tribe [C]'s voting pattern suggested a more [nuanced/moderate/distinctive] position, frequently [agreeing/disagreeing] with statements about [topic_Z] while taking a more [qualified/strong/unique] stance on [related_topic]. Their responses indicated particular concern with [specific_issue], setting them apart from both Tribes [A] and [B].
[If more than three tribes] The remaining tribes showed varying degrees of alignment on different issues. Tribe [D] closely resembled Tribe [A] on matters of [shared_topic] but diverged regarding [point_of_difference]. Meanwhile, Tribe [E] stood out for their distinctive perspective on [unique_topic], taking positions that didn't clearly align with any other tribe.

paragraphInstructions.instruction: For each tribe, provide: - Clear characterization of their distinctive positions - Multiple supporting examples with appropriate citations - Analysis of underlying values or priorities - Comparison with other tribes' positions - Connections between different position statements to reveal coherent tribe perspective

case.description: Tribe that shares positions with different tribes on different issues
Tribe that is internally divided on specific issues

validationRules.rule: All tribe characterizations must be based on multiple statements from data
Each claim requires at least one citation
Tribes must be referenced by actual tribe identifiers from data
